name: Tapeworm / sanitized parasite diet

lead: The tapeworm diet is a fringe idea of deliberately ingesting a tapeworm, or a pill said to contain one, to lose weight quickly and get thinner.

The idea is that a parasite absorbs part of the host's nutrient intake, so fewer calories are taken in. No studies were found testing it as a weight-loss method, and it is not an accepted medical treatment.

paras: It circulates as a historical and online diet notion, usually described through so-called sanitized parasite pills. Because it is not a recognised treatment, there is no established routine or timeline.

Infection with the pork tapeworm Taenia solium can cause cysticercosis, including cysts in the brain, and the resulting neurocysticercosis is described as the leading cause of seizures worldwide; severe cases can cause death. Treatment also needs medical monitoring. Anyone with a suspected infection should see a clinician.

angle.text: The tapeworm diet is a fringe idea in which people look to a parasite to reduce how many calories they absorb, aiming for rapid weight loss and a thinner body. It is not an accepted medical approach and has not been tested as a weight-loss method.

lead: The tapeworm or 'sanitized parasite' diet is the idea of deliberately ingesting a tapeworm, or a product claimed to contain one, so that the parasite absorbs part of the food eaten and the person becomes leaner without cutting calories. The appeal is purely aesthetic: a slimmer body and lower body fat. It is discussed as a fringe weight-loss method and is not an accepted medical treatment.

The notion rests on a real biological fact: intestinal tapeworms live on nutrients in the gut. Reviews describe tapeworm infection as often asymptomatic or mild but occasionally severe, and as able to contribute to anemia and malnutrition [1]. The broad fish tapeworm, for example, absorbs much of the host's dietary vitamin B12 and can cause B12-deficiency anemia [2]. The same sources also list weight loss, abdominal pain and diarrhea among possible symptoms of infection [2][3].

Medical references stress the other side of the parasite. Swallowing eggs of the pork tapeworm Taenia solium can cause cysticercosis, in which cysts form in the brain, eyes and muscles; neurocysticercosis is described as the leading cause of seizures worldwide [4][3][5]. No published study has tested deliberate tapeworm ingestion for weight loss or appearance.
infobox: Weight loss and a leaner body (claimed)

paras: Intestinal cestodes are among the most prevalent human parasites worldwide. Infection is often asymptomatic or mild, and heavy or prolonged infection can contribute to anemia and malnutrition; it is most prevalent in resource-poor countries [1]. The broad fish tapeworm Diphyllobothrium latum is acquired from raw or undercooked freshwater fish and, because it absorbs dietary vitamin B12, can cause megaloblastic or pernicious anemia; treatment involves antiparasitic drugs and B12 [2].
Taenia infection is linked with eating undercooked beef or pork and may cause abdominal symptoms, with segments visible in stool [3].

Humans can acquire cysticercosis by swallowing T. solium eggs in contaminated food or water. Cysts in the brain can cause seizures, headaches, raised intracranial pressure, hydrocephalus, meningitis and, in severe cases, death [4].
Treatment itself needs careful monitoring because dying cysts can trigger inflammation, particularly in the brain [4].

Neurocysticercosis is the most common helminthic infection of the central nervous system worldwide, with seizures the most common presentation and headache, focal deficits, raised intracranial pressure and cognitive decline also reported; imaging is central to diagnosis and cysticidal drugs have improved the prognosis for most patients [5].
No studies found testing deliberate tapeworm ingestion for weight loss or appearance.
